01-send-welcome-email.name: User Welcome Onboarding

01-send-welcome-email.coreLogic: Creates test user data (name and email), then sends personalized welcome email highlighting FairTix's anti-bot fair queuing system, transparent pricing, human verification requirements, and resale caps. Guides user toward account verification as the next action.

The email content reveals a business model focused on 'fair queuing' (no speed advantages), transparent pricing, human verification, and capped resale prices (face value + 20% max). 03-support-classifier.name: Support Ticket Classifier
03-support-classifier.description: AI-powered classification system for FairTix customer support messages. Routes incoming tickets into six categories (FAQ, Account/Verification, Payment/Billing, Technical/Bug, Resale/Transfer, Feedback) and assesses sentiment to prioritize response urgency.
03-support-classifier.trigger: Manual execution for processing existing Gmail support messages with 'Support Request' subject line
03-support-classifier.coreLogic: Retrieves Gmail messages marked as support requests → feeds message content to Claude AI with detailed classification prompt → categorizes by support type and sentiment → writes classification results to Google Sheets for team routing and tracking.
03-support-classifier.businessContext: FairTix operates a fair ticket marketplace requiring structured support routing. The six categories reveal their business model: FAQ (general marketplace education), Account/Verification (user onboarding friction), Payment/Billing (transaction issues), Technical/Bug (platform stability), Resale/Transfer (their core value proposition), and Feedback (product development input). The sentiment analysis indicates they prioritize response urgency based on customer emotional state, suggesting a customer experience focus.
sideEffects: Updates Google Sheets with ticket classifications
Creates structured support pipeline data
Enables category-based team routing

impactProposal.reasoning: Support ticket routing is critical for customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. This workflow transforms unstructured support chaos into organized queues, enabling specialized team responses. For a marketplace, support quality directly impacts user trust and transaction volume.

03-support-classifier.businessBrief: Transforms incoming support chaos into organized category queues — the intelligence layer that routes customer issues to the right specialist team for faster resolution.
03-support-classifier.timeSavingsEstimate: ~2-3 minutes per ticket at scale — replaces manual reading, categorization, and routing decisions. With 25+ tickets per batch, saves 50-75 minutes of manual triage work. Confidence: benchmark-based.
03-support-classifier.revenueImpactEstimate: Indirect but significant — faster support resolution reduces churn and enables transaction recovery. Each misrouted payment issue could delay refunds; each missed technical bug affects platform trust. Confidence: benchmark-based.
03-support-classifier.failureImpact: Support tickets flow into an undifferentiated queue. Specialists receive random ticket types outside their expertise. Response times increase as agents read entire messages to understand issues. Customer frustration builds from generic responses to specialized problems. Payment disputes escalate when billing issues aren't fast-tracked.
03-support-classifier.dataIn: Gmail support messages containing customer name, email, subject, and message body describing their issue or question.
03-support-classifier.dataOut: Structured classification data: category, sentiment, confidence score, rationale, plus original message metadata for team routing and response tracking.

05-generic-error-workflow.name: Central Error Monitoring & Alerting

05-generic-error-workflow.trigger: Triggered automatically when any linked workflow encounters an execution error or exception.

05-generic-error-workflow.businessContext: This is the operational backbone that enables FairTix to run automated business processes with confidence. Without centralized error monitoring, workflow failures would go unnoticed, causing silent business process breakdowns. The 40 executions indicate this system is actively catching and reporting automation failures across the organization. This reveals FairTix has a sophisticated automation infrastructure that requires operational monitoring — they're running business-critical automations that need immediate attention when they fail.
sideEffects: Creates email alerts in operations inbox
Generates audit trail of automation failures
Enables operational incident response

impactProposal.reasoning: This workflow is the safety net for all other automations. The 15% failure rate across executions shows it's actively preventing silent automation failures that would otherwise damage customer experience and operations.
